mainTopic: Whether רבי יהודה's "אימתי" explains or disputes; the shared עירוב תחומין, its purpose and timing (ברירה); and which child is covered by his mother's עירוב
overview: This amud first settles a contradiction from the previous discussion: שמואל and רבי יהושע בן לוי are two different אמוראים, so they may simply disagree. The גמרא then examines רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that רבי יהודה's "אימתי" and "במה" always explain the חכמים. רבי יוחנן says "אימתי" explains but "במה" disagrees. The גמרא challenges "אימתי" from the case of disqualified witnesses, where a ברייתא has the חכמים disqualify a gambler even if he has another job. It answers that this strict view follows רבי יהודה in the name of רבי טרפון, who holds that a commitment made in doubt is not real, as in the case of an uncertain נזירות. That makes a gambler's winnings like stolen money. After the הדרן closing פרק חלון, a new משנה teaches how one person makes an עירוב תחומין for the whole town, and that each person must accept it before nightfall. The גמרא brings רב יוסף's rule that such an עירוב is only for a מצוה, and רב אשי's reading that 'while still day' is about being informed, so the משנה does not prove אין ברירה. Finally, רב אסי rules that a six-year-old goes out with his mother's עירוב. A ברייתא ties this to whether the child still needs his mother, which the גמרא defines and dates to about age four or five, setting up a challenge to רב אסי that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two different אמוראים may simply disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers a contradiction from the previous discussion. The two opinions belong to two different people, so there is no real contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you raising a contradiction between one person and another? One Sage (שמואל) holds that רבי יהודה and the חכמים disagree, and the other Sage (רבי יהושע בן לוי) holds that they do not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles an apparent contradiction from the earlier discussion. It points out that the two statements come from two different אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A contradiction only counts as a problem when one person seems to say two opposite things. Here שמואל holds that רבי יהודה argues with the חכמים, and רבי יהושע בן לוי holds that he only explains them. They are simply two opinions, so nothing needs to be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Are you pitting one person against another? (a contradiction between two different people is not a real problem)
One master holds
They disagree

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a standard גמרא tool. When two opinions clash and they come from two different people, the גמרא simply says they argue.

phrases.english: Are you raising a contradiction between one man and another man?!
phrases.notes: He's not really asking; he means there's no real contradiction here.

phrases.english: One master holds that they disagree,
and the other master holds that they do not disagree.
phrases.notes: This refers to רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the contradiction raised on the previous amud, from the previous part of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution split: the two statements belong to two different אמוראים who argue.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner thought שמואל's view and רבי יהושע בן לוי's view had to fit together.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are separate opinions. שמואל says רבי יהודה argues, and רבי יהושע בן לוי says he only explains.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule for "when" and "in what case"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to study רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement directly. He says רבי יהודה's "אימתי" and "במה" always come to explain the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Every place where רבי יהודה says "when" or "in what case" in our משנה, he only means to explain the words of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says "גופא", which means "now let us look at the statement itself". It then quotes רבי יהושע בן לוי's full rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהושע בן לוי, both phrases are signals of explanation and never of argument. So when רבי יהודה adds a condition with these words, the חכמים agree with that condition.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: a return to examine a statement that was quoted earlier in passing
When? (introduces a condition)
In what case? (introduces a limit)
To explain

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Every place where Rabbi Yehuda said
"when" or "in what case" in our Mishna,
it is only to explain the words of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the statement that was mentioned in Step 1 and now examines it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "אימתי" and "במה" from רבי יהודה both mean he is explaining the חכמים, not arguing with them.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן splits the two phrases
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says "אימתי" explains, but "במה" means רבי יהודה is disagreeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: "When" is to explain, and "in what case" is to disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא, רבי יוחנן, gives a different rule from רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן agrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי about "אימתי". But he holds that "במה" shows a real מחלוקת. Both of them agree that "אימתי" means explaining, and the next steps will challenge exactly that shared point.

keyTerms.meaning: To disagree

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן disagrees about "אימתי". Both אמוראים agree that "אימתי" means explaining. They only argue about "במה".

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
"When" is to explain,
and "in what case" is to disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing rule to רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule in Step 2.

steps.title: Challenge: a משנה about disqualified witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether "אימתי" really always means explaining. It begins quoting a משנה that lists people who cannot be witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is "when" really to explain? But we learned in a משנה: These are the people who are disqualified: one who plays with dice, one who lends with interest, those who race pigeons, and merchants of שביעית produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the shared view that "אימתי" always explains. It starts by quoting a משנה whose next line will be the test case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי יוחנן agreed that "אימתי" means explaining, so this challenge hits both of them. The list here is the first half of the משנה, the opinion of the חכמים. רבי יהודה's "אימתי" comment on this list comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה (introduces a source used to challenge)
People who are disqualified (here: from being witnesses)
One who gambles with dice
Pigeon racers who bet on the races
People who trade in produce of the Sabbatical year

phrases.english: And is "when" really to explain?
But didn't we learn:
And these are the disqualified ones:
phrases.notes: They are disqualified from giving testimony. The משנה is in סנהדרין 24b.

phrases.english: one who plays with dice,
and one who lends with interest,
and those who fly pigeons,
phrases.notes: They bet on which pigeon wins.

phrases.english: and merchants of Sabbatical-year produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the point that Steps 2 and 3 share: that "אימתי" means explaining.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim, held by both רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי יוחנן, that "אימתי" always signals explanation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It brings a משנה where רבי יהודה says "אימתי". The גמרא will go on to show that in this case he actually disagrees with the חכמים.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's "when" in that Mishna
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues with רבי יהודה using "אימתי". He says these people are disqualified only if this is their only occupation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When is this so? When he has no occupation except this one. But if he has an occupation other than this one, he is a valid witness.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the quote that the challenge is built on: רבי יהודה's "אימתי" comment. The גמרא is setting up the proof, which continues next, that here "אימתי" really means disagreeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה limits the disqualification to someone who earns his living only from these activities. If this limit is a real argument with the חכמים, then "אימתי" does not always mean explaining. That would contradict both אמוראים.

keyTerms.meaning: An occupation or trade
Valid (fit to serve as a witness)
At a time when / in a case where

steps.confusionAlert: This line is still part of the quoted משנה, not the גמרא speaking. The actual proof that רבי יהודה is arguing here comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: When?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אוּמָּנוּת אֶלָּא הִיא,
phrases.english: At a time when he has no occupation except this,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ לוֹ אוּמָּנוּת שֶׁלֹּא הִיא —
phrases.english: but if he has an occupation other than this,
this one is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה quote that Step 4 began. This is the exact case of "אימתי" that the challenge is built on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here רבי יהודה's "אימתי" adds an occupation condition that seems to argue with the חכמים' full disqualification. The proof that it is a real argument continues next.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the חכמים disqualifying a gambler in every case
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is completed. A ברייתא says the חכמים disqualify the gambler even if he has another job. That suggests רבי יהודה's "אימתי" was a disagreement, not an explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches about this משנה: The חכמים say, whether he has no job other than this one, or whether he has a different job, he is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to disprove the rule that "אימתי" always explains the חכמים. This is the punch line of the challenge that began in steps 4 and 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה said the gambler is disqualified only when gambling is his only job. The ברייתא shows the חכמים saying he is disqualified either way. So the חכמים clearly disagree with רבי יהודה, even though he used the word "אימתי".

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught about it (a ברייתא commenting on the משנה)
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
A job, profession, or occupation
Disqualified (here, from being a witness)

steps.confusionAlert: Steps 4 and 5 only quoted the משנה. The actual problem appears here: the ברייתא shows the חכמים ruling more strictly than רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: And it was taught about it in a baraita:
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אוּמָּנוּת אֶלָּא הִיא,
phrases.english: whether he has no occupation other than this one,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אוּמָּנוּת שֶׁלֹּא הִיא —
phrases.english: or whether he has an occupation other than this one,
this person is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge by adding a ברייתא to the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule (step 2) and רבי יוחנן's rule (step 3) that "אימתי" always explains the חכמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here רבי יהודה says "אימתי", yet the ברייתא shows the חכמים disagreeing with him. So "אימתי" does not always mean explaining.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה's teaching in the name of רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: The view in the ברייתא is not that of the חכמים of the משנה. It follows the principle רבי יהודה taught in the name of רבי טרפון. So the חכמים of the משנה can still agree with רבי יהודה's "אימתי".
steps.simpleTranslation: That view in the ברייתא follows what רבי יהודה said in the name of רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The strict view in the ברייתא comes from a different source, not from the חכמים of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict view (disqualified even with another job) depends on a special principle taught by רבי יהודה in the name of רבי טרפון. The חכמים of the משנה do not hold that principle. They can agree with רבי יהודה, so his "אימתי" still works as an explanation and the rule survives.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (that teaching)
A תנא whose teaching רבי יהודה passes on

phrases.english: That opinion is of Rabbi Yehuda,
who said it in the name of Rabbi Tarfon.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by assigning the ברייתא's view to a different source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning authorship: the conflicting view belongs to a different source, not to the חכמים of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's חכמים are the same as the משנה's חכמים, so they disagree with רבי יהודה's "אימתי".
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה's teaching in the name of רבי טרפון. The חכמים of the משנה agree with רבי יהודה, and "אימתי" still explains.

steps.title: רבי טרפון's teaching: an uncertain נזירות does not take effect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the source. רבי יהודה said in the name of רבי טרפון that when each person's נזירות depends on an uncertain outcome, neither becomes a נזיר. נזירות requires a clear, definite acceptance.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה said in the name of רבי טרפון, neither one of them is ever a נזיר, because נזירות only takes effect with a clear, definite statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the actual teaching of רבי טרפון that the answer in step 7 relied on. The next step will explain how it connects to gambling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case involves people whose נזירות depended on something uncertain, like a bet whose result is unclear. רבי טרפון rules that none of them is a נזיר. A vow of נזירות needs a clear acceptance (הפלאה), and an uncertain condition is not clear.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
A person who vowed to avoid wine, haircuts, and impurity from the dead
The state or vow of being a נזיר
A clear, explicit statement of a vow
Ever, in any case

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said in the name of Rabbi Tarfon:
neither one of them is ever a nazirite,
because there is no naziriteship without a clear, explicit declaration.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source of the teaching mentioned in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה in the name of רבי טרפון holds a principle about uncertain commitments.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about נזירות that depends on an uncertain outcome.

steps.title: The shared logic: no full commitment when the outcome is uncertain
steps.stepSummary: From the נזיר case, the גמרא learns that a person does not truly commit when he is unsure of the result. The same applies to a gambler: he does not fully give away his money, so the winner holds money that was not truly given, like a thief. That is why רבי טרפון's view disqualifies every gambler.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that since he is unsure whether he will be a נזיר or not, he does not truly bind himself. Here too, since the gambler does not know whether he will win or lose, he does not fully decide to transfer the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from the נזיר teaching and applies it to gambling. This explains why the ברייתא disqualifies a gambler even if he has another job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The common idea is that an uncertain commitment is not a real commitment. A loser in gambling never fully agreed to give his money away, so the winner is taking money that was not truly given, which is a kind of stealing. Stealing disqualifies a witness no matter what job he has, so this view is stricter than the משנה's חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: We see from this, evidently
Binds himself, truly commits
Here too (applying the same logic)
Fully decides and transfers ownership

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's "אימתי" can still be an explanation. The strict ברייתא follows רבי טרפון's principle that an uncertain commitment is not real, which makes the gambler's winnings like stolen money. The חכמים of the משנה do not use that principle, so they agree with רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is discussing the laws of נזיר for their own sake. The נזיר case is brought only to show a principle that is then applied to the gambler.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that an uncertain commitment does not fully take effect, is the basis for the well-known concept of אסמכתא in monetary law.

phrases.english: Evidently, since he is in doubt

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָזִיר אִי לָא נָזִיר הוּא —
phrases.english: whether he is a nazirite or not a nazirite,
he does not bind himself.
Here too:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא יָדַע אִי קָנֵי אִי לָא קָנֵי —
phrases.english: since he does not know whether he will acquire or not acquire,
he does not fully resolve to transfer ownership.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a principle from the נזיר ברייתא in step 8 and applies it to the gambler.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא's strict view on gamblers comes from רבי טרפון's principle about uncertain commitments.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference from the נזיר case: doubt prevents a full commitment.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק חלון
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the chapter called חלון.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter חלון.
steps.whatsHappening: This line formally closes the previous chapter, פרק חלון. It is not part of any argument. It only marks a chapter boundary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional farewell said at the end of every chapter. It means 'we will return to you,' expressing the hope to learn this chapter again. The next line begins a completely new chapter with its own משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the formula said at the end of a chapter
'Window': the name of the chapter now ending

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter 'Window'
phrases.notes: This is the traditional line said when finishing a chapter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the previous chapter. It does not connect to the earlier argument.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק חלון is complete, and a new chapter begins.

steps.title: How to make a shared עירוב תחומין for the whole town
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that one person places a barrel of food and declares it is for all townspeople going to a house of mourning or a wedding feast.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do people join together in an עירוב תחומין? A person places the barrel of food and says: 'This is for all the people of my town, for anyone who will go to a house of mourning or to a wedding feast.'
steps.whatsHappening: The new chapter's משנה opens by explaining how one person can make a single עירוב תחומין that works for many people. He places food and declares who it is for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person may walk only 2,000 אמות beyond his town on שבת. An עירוב תחומין, which is food placed at a spot before שבת, moves his 'home base' there. Here one person makes it on behalf of everyone who needs to go to a mourner or a wedding.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being studied
Joining together in an עירוב for the שבת boundary
The 2,000-אמה walking limit on שבת
A house of mourning, where one goes to comfort mourners
A wedding feast

steps.confusionAlert: This is an עירוב תחומין, which extends how far you may walk. It is not an עירוב חצרות, which allows carrying between courtyards. 'משתתפין' here refers to boundaries, not alleyways.

phrases.english: MISHNA: How does one join together in Shabbat boundaries?
He places the barrel of food, and says:
This is for all the people of my town,
for anyone who will go to a house of mourning
or to a wedding feast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One person can make an עירוב תחומין for the townspeople by placing food and declaring it is for those going to a mourner or a wedding.

steps.title: Accepting the עירוב must happen before nightfall
steps.stepSummary: Only someone who accepted the עירוב while it was still day may rely on it. Accepting it after dark does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone who accepted it upon himself while it was still day is permitted. If he accepted it after dark, he is forbidden, because one cannot make an עירוב after dark.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a timing rule. A person must decide to use this עירוב before שבת begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the food was placed for everyone, each person must accept it before nightfall. An עירוב works by setting your place at the start of שבת. A decision made after שבת has started comes too late.

keyTerms.meaning: While it is still day, before שבת starts
After it gets dark, once שבת has begun
Making an עירוב

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם — מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: And anyone who accepted it upon himself while it was still day is permitted;
if after dark, he is forbidden.
For one may not make an eruv after dark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a timing condition to the shared עירוב described in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may rely on the shared עירוב only if he accepted it before nightfall.

steps.title: רב יוסף: עירוב תחומין only for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that an עירוב תחומין may be made only for the sake of a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: One may make an עירוב only for a מצוה purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling from רב יוסף. He limits עירוב תחומין to מצוה needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף adds a restriction. You may not make an עירוב תחומין just to take a walk or for a personal errand. It must be for something like comforting a mourner or celebrating a wedding.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
The אמורא who states this rule
A מצוה purpose

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic limit on when an עירוב תחומין may be used, and it is the focus of the discussion that follows.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yosef said:
One may make an eruv only for a מצוה purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אֵין מְעָרְבִין אֶלָּא לִדְבַר מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's first statement on the משנה, adding a limiting rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב תחומין may be made only for a מצוה.

steps.title: Why does רב יוסף need to say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב יוסף adds, since the משנה already mentions only מצוה cases: a house of mourning and a wedding feast.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned in the משנה: 'for anyone who will go to a house of mourning or to a wedding feast'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף. It claims his rule is already stated in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's examples are both מצוות. That seems to show that an עירוב is only for a מצוה. If so, רב יוסף's statement looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is he teaching us?': asks what a statement adds
'We already learned it' in a משנה

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned: For anyone who will go
to a house of mourning or to a wedding feast!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב יוסף's statement in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's rule that an עירוב is only for a מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already lists only מצוה cases, so the rule seems redundant.

steps.title: The משנה may only describe the usual case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought the משנה's מצוה examples were just the typical situation, so רב יוסף teaches that a מצוה is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that the משנה is just describing the usual situation. So he teaches us that it really must be a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף. The משנה's examples alone do not prove that a מצוה is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People usually go far on שבת only for important events like mourning or weddings. So the משנה might have mentioned these simply because they are common, not because they are required. רב יוסף makes it clear that the limit is a real rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have said': introduces a mistaken assumption
'It teaches the usual way of things': the example is typical, not a requirement

steps.whatToRemember: An עירוב תחומין may be made only for a מצוה. The משנה's examples alone could have been read as just typical cases, so רב יוסף states the rule explicitly.

phrases.english: You might have said:
it teaches the usual way of things;
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה's examples as possibly typical rather than required
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה mentions מצוה cases only because they are the common reason to make an עירוב, and an optional trip would also be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יוסף teaches that a מצוה purpose is truly required for an עירוב תחומין.

steps.title: Does the משנה's phrase prove there is no ברירה?
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's words 'while still day,' the גמרא infers that the משנה holds אין ברירה. If ברירה worked, a decision made on שבת should count retroactively.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says only one who accepted the עירוב while it was still day may use it. Learn from this that there is no ברירה. If there were ברירה, then once he decides on שבת, it should be revealed retroactively that already while it was day he wanted it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase again and draws a conclusion from it. The phrase seems to show that the משנה rejects the idea of ברירה (retroactive clarification).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עירוב was placed for 'whoever wants to go.' If a person only decides on שבת that he wants to go, ברירה would say his decision reveals that he was included from the start, before שבת. Since the משנה requires acceptance while it was still day, it seems the משנה holds אין ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was 'really' true earlier
Learn from this (introduces an inference)
Retroactively, looking back to an earlier time
He was content with it, he wanted it

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'while still day' was already explained in step 12. The גמרא is not repeating itself here. It quotes the same words again for a new purpose: to draw a conclusion about ברירה.
steps.whyThisMatters: ברירה is a major principle that appears all over ש״ס. If this משנה really proved אין ברירה, it would be an important source.

phrases.english: 'And anyone who accepted it upon himself while it was still day.'
Learn from this: there is no retroactive clarification,
for if there were retroactive clarification,
let the matter be revealed retroactively
that already while it was day he was content with it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's phrase from step 12 and draws a principle out of it
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה holds אין ברירה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's requirement to accept the עירוב 'מבעוד יום'. If יש ברירה, a decision made on שבת would reveal retroactively that he wanted it while it was still day, so the requirement would be pointless.

steps.title: רב אשי: The משנה is about being informed, not deciding
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that 'while still day' means the person was told about the עירוב before שבת. If he knew about it, he may decide later, so ברירה can still work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The משנה is teaching the difference between 'they informed him' and 'they did not inform him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. He reinterprets the משנה's phrase so that it no longer proves אין ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב אשי, the person does not need to decide before שבת. He only needs to know about the עירוב before שבת. If he knew, his later decision on שבת works through ברירה. If no one told him, there is nothing to clarify retroactively, so the עירוב does not help him.

keyTerms.meaning: They informed him (that the עירוב was placed)
It (the משנה) is teaching

steps.whatToRemember: 'While still day' means the person knew about the עירוב before שבת. It does not mean he had already decided to use it. So this משנה does not prove אין ברירה.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It teaches the case of 'they informed him' versus 'they did not inform him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the inference of step 16
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'While still day' means he had to decide before שבת, which implies אין ברירה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'While still day' means he had to be informed before שבת, and ברירה can still work for his later decision

steps.title: רב אסי: A six-year-old is included in his mother's עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי rules that a six-year-old child may walk on שבת based on his mother's עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: A six-year-old child may go out by means of his mother's עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling. A young child does not need his own עירוב because he is included in his mother's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small child is attached to his mother, so her עירוב covers him as well. רב אסי sets the cutoff at a fixed age: six.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child
Goes out, may walk (based on the עירוב)
His mother's עירוב

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
A six-year-old child
may go out by means of his mother's eruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: who is included in someone else's עירוב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A six-year-old child is covered by his mother's עירוב

steps.title: A ברייתא ties the rule to whether the child needs his mother
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a child goes out with his mother's עירוב only if he still needs his mother. This seems to contradict רב אסי's fixed age of six.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: A child who needs his mother goes out by means of his mother's עירוב. A child who does not need his mother does not go out by means of his mother's עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אסי with a ברייתא. The ברייתא makes the rule depend on the child's need for his mother, not on his age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי gave a set age of six. The ברייתא uses a different test: is the child still dependent on his mother? A six-year-old may already be independent, so the ברייתא would exclude him while רב אסי includes him.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
Needs his mother, is still dependent on her

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A child who needs his mother
goes out by means of his mother's eruv,
and one who does not need his mother
does not go out by means of his mother's eruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אסי's ruling from step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's fixed age of six
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's test is dependence on the mother, not age. A six-year-old who is already independent would be excluded by the ברייתא but included by רב אסי.

steps.title: A parallel משנה about סוכה uses the same test
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that a משנה about סוכה uses the same phrase: a child who no longer needs his mother is obligated in סוכה. This sets up a definition of that phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we also learned a similar case regarding סוכה: A child who does not need his mother is obligated in סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel source that uses the same test of 'needing his mother.' It is setting up the next move, which will define what this phrase means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'does not need his mother' also appears in the laws of סוכה, so its meaning there can tell us its meaning here. Once that meaning is defined, we can check whether it fits a six-year-old, as רב אסי ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
Like this, in a similar way
Obligated to sit in the סוכה (for training in מצוות)

phrases.english: And we also learned regarding sukka
something similar to this:
A child who does not need his mother
is obligated in sukka.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי סוּכָּה כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel source for the ברייתא's test from step 19, preparing a definition
steps.raayaObject: The test of 'needing his mother' used in step 19
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוכה about a child who does not need his mother
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's ruling that a six-year-old goes out with his mother's עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סוכה משנה uses the same test of 'needing his mother'. The discussion of that test in the next steps fixes an age of about four or five, which is younger than רב אסי's six.

steps.title: Which child no longer needs his mother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion of the סוכה משנה, which asked how to define 'a child who no longer needs his mother.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: Which child counts as one who does not need his mother?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes an earlier discussion that asked what the phrase 'a child who does not need his mother' means. This sets up the definitions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase appears both in the ברייתא about עירוב and in the סוכה משנה. If we can define it, we can test whether it fits רב אסי's fixed age of six.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (introduces an earlier discussion of a source)
A minor, a child
Who does not need his mother

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
phrases.notes: This is talking about the משנה from סוכה that was quoted back in Step 20.

phrases.english: And which child is one who does not need his mother?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: וְאֵיזֶהוּ קָטָן שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לְאִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the phrase from the סוכה משנה (Step 20) and asks for its definition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical definition of a child who no longer needs his mother.

steps.title: First definition: he cleans himself
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ינאי define it as a child who goes to the bathroom and does not need his mother to clean him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: Any child who relieves himself and his mother does not have to wipe him.
steps.whatsHappening: The students of רבי ינאי give the first answer: a child is independent once he can clean himself after using the bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This definition is based on a real stage of growing up, not a fixed age. Different children reach it at different times.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (students) of רבי ינאי said
Relieves himself, uses the bathroom
Wipes him, cleans him

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
Any child who relieves himself
and his mother does not wipe him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A child who can clean himself after using the bathroom no longer needs his mother.

steps.title: Second definition: he does not call for his mother
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש defines it as a child who wakes up and does not call 'Mother.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: Any child who wakes up and does not call out 'Mother.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different answer: a child is independent once he wakes up without calling for his mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another sign of independence, also based on the child's behavior. As written, though, it sounds too strict, and the גמרא will question it next.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, an אמורא of ארץ ישראל
Wakes up
Mother (what the child calls out)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Any child who wakes up
and does not call out 'Mother.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: כׇּל שֶׁנֵּיעוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the question in Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A child who wakes up and does not call for his mother no longer needs her.

steps.title: Even older children call their mother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: older children also call 'Mother' when they wake up, so this cannot be the test.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think it means calling 'Mother' once? Even older children call out like that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's definition as it was just worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If calling 'Mother' even once meant a child still needs her, then even big children would count as dependent. That cannot be right, so the wording must mean something narrower.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (signals that a reading is impossible)
Older children
Also call out

phrases.english: 'Mother' — can it enter your mind?
Older children also call out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of ריש לקיש's definition in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's definition: a child who does not call 'Mother.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Older children also call their mothers, so this test would make almost every child dependent.

steps.title: He means calling 'Mother, Mother' again and again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords ריש לקיש: a child who wakes up and does not keep calling 'Mother, Mother.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: Any child who wakes up from his sleep and does not keep calling 'Mother, Mother.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of ריש לקיש's definition so that it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real sign of dependence is a child who keeps calling and will not get up until his mother comes. A single call is normal at any age, so it does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (introduces corrected wording)
From his sleep

steps.confusionAlert: The fix does not change ריש לקיש's idea. It only explains that 'calling Mother' means calling again and again, not one call.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Any child who wakes up from his sleep
and does not call 'Mother, Mother.'
phrases.notes: The repeated call shows the child cannot manage without her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 24 by rewording Step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Calling 'Mother' even once shows the child still needs her.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a child who keeps calling 'Mother, Mother' still needs her.

steps.title: At what age does this usually happen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how old a child usually is when he no longer needs his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how old is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what age matches these signs. This sets up an age that can be compared with רב אסי's age of six.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The definitions so far describe behavior. Now the גמרא wants an actual age, which can be measured against רב אסי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much? (here: at what age?)

phrases.english: And how old?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the stage, asks for the typical age.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The usual age at which a child stops needing his mother.

steps.title: About four or five years old
steps.stepSummary: The answer: around four or five, which seems to clash with רב אסי's six.
steps.simpleTranslation: About four, or about five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a child usually stops needing his mother at about four or five. This sets up a problem for רב אסי, who said a six-year-old still uses his mother's עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some children become independent at four and some at five. If even a five-year-old may no longer need his mother, how can רב אסי let a six-year-old rely on her עירוב?

keyTerms.meaning: About four years old
About five years old

steps.whatToRemember: A child who no longer needs his mother is one who cleans himself (דבי רבי ינאי) or wakes up without calling 'Mother, Mother' again and again (ריש לקיש). This usually happens at about four or five, which puts pressure on רב אסי's age of six.
steps.whyThisMatters: This age answer sets up the next challenge against רב אסי's ruling about a six-year-old and his mother's עירוב.

phrases.english: About four,
about five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 26 and implicitly sharpens the problem against רב אסי (Step 18).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: About four or five years old, depending on the child.
